written: 2026-10-30, before any headline was fetched or scored
question: Does the tone of each team's headlines in the 7 days before an NFL game predict the result beyond the closing line?
data: Google News RSS search "<full team name>" for kickoff-7d .. kickoff+1d, 2023-2025 regular season + playoffs; only items published >= 2 h before kickoff count; duplicate titles count once
score: VADER compound score of each title (vaderSentiment, default lexicon). Per team-game: tone = mean compound; neg_share = share of titles with compound <= -0.05; volume = log(1 + count)
features: home minus away of tone, neg_share and volume

targets.cover: home margin minus the closing home spread (nflverse spread_line: home margin + spread_line > 0 = home covers)

tests.T1_cover: OLS of cover margin on diff_tone (one feature, no other tuning). Dev = 2023 (look freely). Holdout = 2024-25, run once. Pass: holdout slope has the dev sign and one-sided p < 0.025, and |slope| x SD(diff_tone) >= 0.25 pts
tests.T3_volume_total: OLS of total residual on (home + away volume): media-heavy games go over/under? Same pass rule
tests.T4_rule: only if T1 or T2 pass: bet the side the tone favours when |diff| is in the top 20% of 2023's distribution, at the closing line, -110; holdout ROI one-sided p < 0.05 over all 2024-25 qualifiers

multiple_testing: 3 primary tests; each needs one-sided p < 0.025 (Bonferroni-ish 0.05/2 per direction-fixed test)
not_tested: No refits, no lexicon changes, no other windows after seeing the holdout. A different design = a new pre-registration.
